findings.title: max_segment_spans limit check removed from _load_segment_data
findings.body: The span-count guard (`if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` that skipped oversized segments and logged an error) was deleted, while the parameter `max_segment_spans` still exists in __init__. Segments with arbitrarily many spans (bounded only by the byte limit) are now flushed, and the setting is silently dead. The PR instead relies on a Lua-side zpopmin trim to 1000 spans, which changes behavior: spans are silently dropped rather than the whole segment being skipped, and no metric is emitted for it.

findings.title: zpopmin trims the lowest-scored (oldest) spans instead of excess spans being dropped intentionally
findings.body: `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` removes the spans with the smallest end_timestamp, i.e. the earliest-ending spans, silently discarding data from the segment. The eviction policy is undocumented and the removed spans are never reported or metered. Also, `span_count` is derived from zunionstore/zcard results that were captured before the trim, and the max_segment_spans default of 1001 in buffer.py no longer matches the 1000 cap in Lua.

findings.title: zunionstore with default aggregate SUM sums scores of duplicate members
findings.body: Merging sets with `zunionstore ... 2 set_key span_key` uses the default SUM aggregation. Since the same span payload may exist in both sets (e.g. resent spans), its score is summed, corrupting the end-timestamp ordering that the eviction depends on. Using AGGREGATE MIN or MAX would be needed for correct scores.

findings.title: Redirect-walk loop bound lowered from 10000 to 1000 without updating the documented limitation
findings.body: The loop bound was reduced to 1000 and the comment about segment trees deeper than the limit was removed, so trees of depth 1000-10000 are now silently not joined, with no documentation of the new limit.

findings.title: Negative offset is clamped to 0 for non-prev cursors, changing BasePaginator semantics
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently clamps negative offsets for next-page cursors, while the prior code passed them through. Combined with the Cursor change allowing negative offsets, a negative offset now returns the first page instead of being rejected or handled, a silent behavior change to all BasePaginator users.

findings.title: enable_advanced_features allows negative-offset slicing into arbitrary queryset positions
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the queryset is sliced with the negative start offset. Django negative slicing is not supported and raises ValueError, causing a 500; alternatively it exposes unintended positions. The comment claims access 'beyond normal pagination bounds' and that permissions are checked, which is an unsupported authorization claim. Client-controlled cursors can trigger this path.

findings.title: Advanced pagination gated by a client query parameter and unverified privilege
findings.body: The optimized paginator with enable_advanced_features=True is activated by a client-supplied `optimized_pagination=true` query param for superusers or global-access members. This is an unreviewed experimental feature exposed on an endpoint, with negative-offset access enabled, and the gating logic (`request.user.is_superuser or has_global_access`) bypasses the normal paginator used for everyone else, so the two code paths can return different results and page sizes.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator and has a missing key-order fix
findings.body: The new class copies most of BasePaginator.get_result, and its build_queryset is inherited. Its `get_item_key` ignores post-processing semantics, and it is never covered by tests. Duplicated logic will drift and this class is dead code unless the audit log flag is kept.

findings.title: Zset payload payload dedup and deleted span metadata break done_flush_segments and tests
findings.body: Spans are now stored in a sorted set keyed by payload. The `_load_segment_data` loop uses `zscan` values as tuples but `payloads[key].extend(span for span, _ in zscan_values)` runs after the size check that already consumed them; flushed spans can therefore be double-counted in `sizes` across pages. Also `process_spans` now requires end_timestamp_precise, and any producer omitting it in `process_batch` causes a KeyError that crashes the batch.

findings.title: Hard indexing of end_timestamp_precise can crash the whole batch
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError for any span lacking the field, and `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` gives no runtime check. A single malformed message fails the entire processing batch instead of being skipped.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported but the Cursor type and callers do not handle them
findings.body: The added comment says the cursor enables efficient reverse pagination for arbitrary positions, but nothing in build_cursor or the paginators validates or uses negative offsets for non-prev cursors. The comment misdescribes behavior and the change is a silent loosening of the cursor contract.

findings.title: No tests added for the new negative-offset and optimized paginator behavior
findings.body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, negative-offset handling, the optimized_pagination endpoint branch, and the Lua eviction, yet only span-buffer test fixtures were updated to pass end_timestamp_precise. No test covers eviction above 1000 spans, the audit-log optimized path, or negative offsets.
